item.title: Journal Meeting: Enhancing cognitive function through blood flow restriction: An effective resistance exercise modality for middle-aged women
item.description:
Presentation Highlights / 報告精華

Introduction & Rationale

Cognitive decline progresses more rapidly in women than in men, with a higher prevalence of neurodegenerative diseases observed in females. While exercise has been shown to enhance cognitive function through the upregulation of neurotrophic factors (like BDNF, VEGF, and IGF-1), high-load resistance exercise may not be suitable for all populations, particularly middle-aged women. Low-load resistance exercise with blood flow restriction (LLBFR) has emerged as an effective alternative.

Key Findings

  • Cognitive Performance: Only the LLBFR condition showed significant improvements in Color-Word Stroop Task (CWST) reaction time, with no changes in error rates, indicating enhanced cognitive performance.
  • Neurotrophic Factors: Serum BDNF and VEGF levels increased significantly following both LLBFR and moderate-load resistance exercise (MLRE). IGF-1 levels remained unchanged across conditions.
  • Metabolic Responses: Increases in lactate concentrations were positively correlated with changes in BDNF and VEGF.

Practical Application

A single session of LLBFR successfully improves cognitive function and upregulates key neurotrophic factors (BDNF and VEGF) in middle-aged women. This makes LLBFR an effective and practical intervention for promoting cognitive health in this population.

研究動機與背景

女性認知衰退的速度較男性更快，且神經退化性疾病的盛行率也較高。雖然運動能透過提升神經營養因子（如 BDNF、VEGF 和 IGF-1）來改善認知功能，但高負荷阻力訓練並不一定適合所有族群，尤其是中年女性。因此，低負荷血流限制阻力訓練（LLBFR）成為了一種安全且有效的替代方案。

核心發現

  • 認知表現：僅有 LLBFR 組在史楚普色詞測驗（CWST）的反應時間有顯著進步，且錯誤率未增加，顯示認知表現獲得實質提升。
  • 神經營養因子：在執行 LLBFR 與中等負荷阻力訓練（MLRE）後，血清中的 BDNF 與 VEGF 濃度皆顯著上升，而 IGF-1 則無顯著變化。
  • 代謝反應：乳酸濃度的增加與 BDNF 及 VEGF 的變化量呈現正相關。

實務建議

單次低負荷血流限制阻力訓練（LLBFR）即可改善中年女性的認知功能，並提升關鍵的神經營養因子（BDNF 與 VEGF）。這項結果表明，LLBFR 可作為促進該族群認知健康的有效介入策略。

報告資訊

  • Presenter / 報告人: Steve Ying-Chu Chen, Ph.D. candidate
  • Advisor / 指導教授: Yu-Kai Chang (張育愷), Ph.D.
  • Lab / 實驗室: Physical Activity & Cognitive Neuroscience Lab (PACN Lab), NTNU

item.title: The 16th ISSP World Congress: Acute Resistance Exercise and Inhibitory Control
item.description:
Certificate of Attendance: Mr. Ying-Chu Chen participated in The 16th ISSP World Congress, sponsored by the Shine Tak Foundation and hosted by the Hong Kong Sports Institute between 8 and 12 December 2025.

Presentation Highlights: In his oral presentation, “The Influence of Acute Resistance Exercise Volume on Inhibitory Control: A Randomized Controlled Trial,” Ying-Chu Chen discussed the relationship between resistance training variables and executive function. The study utilized a randomized controlled design to compare the effects of different exercise intensities with matched total volumes.

Key Findings:

  • Volume Matters: The study concluded that exercise volume might be a key determinant for acute cognitive benefits.
  • Intensity Agnostic: Both low and moderate-intensity resistance exercise protocols resulted in significant improvements in inhibitory control (measured by the Stroop Task) when the total volume was held constant.
  • Physiological Response: Lactate levels increased similarly across exercise groups, suggesting a comparable metabolic response supporting the cognitive gains.
  • Clinical Implication: Low-intensity resistance exercise can be an effective strategy for enhancing cognitive health, especially for populations unable to perform high-intensity training, provided the volume is sufficient.

This research contributes to the growing body of evidence in exercise cognition interaction, offering practical guidelines for exercise prescription aimed at brain health.
